note: Record SHAPES, not bytes (SPEC §10). `examples/vectors.json` pins how a record is serialized; this file pins WHAT A RECORD IS. Every entry in `accept` MUST validate as the stated (type, version). Every entry in `reject` MUST produce the stated `outcome` — and `invalid`, `unsupported-version`, `unknown-type`, `legacy` and `not-a-record` are FIVE outcomes, not two: collapsing an unread record into `valid` reads what the reader does not understand, and collapsing it into `invalid` calls a forward-compatible writer an attacker (SPEC §6.2).
reject_note: The `shape` class is the one a canonicalization vector cannot reach: every one of those records is impeccable JCS I-JSON whose SHAPE is wrong. An implementation that serializes correctly and validates nothing passes examples/vectors.json completely.
